_source: Hand tables, checked 2026-10-23 against Fortson 2010 (ch. 7) and Ringe 2017 (ch. 2); per-form verdicts in raw/books/extract/fortson/diff.jsonl, summarized in docs/morphology.md. Cells list alternatives, primary first. Book spellings without initial laryngeals (eǵ, yós, en, e-, apo) are kept as alternatives. Our laryngeal forms follow Wiktionary/LIV notation. Demonstrative ABL/INS: handbook contracted tósmōd, tóh₁ first (Fortson), Ringe's tósmead, tónoh₁ as alternatives (tier3-t001 review). Anaphoric *h₁e-/*h₁i- (anaphoric_i) from Ringe 2017 p. 56 with Beekes 2011 p. 229; near deictic *ḱo- (deictic_ki) and far *h₁eno- (deictic_eno) have their Hittite-attested cells cited and the rest derived from demonstrative_so like interrogative_kwo (_derived).

interrogative_adv._note: Indeclinable interrogative adverbs and the quantifier 'how many' of the *kʷo-/*kʷi- system (Mallory & Adams 2006 §24.3, Table 24.3). Each key is the English meaning; the list is the form, primary first. why and when are case forms of the pronouns used adverbially (interrogative_kwi/n/ACC.SG, interrogative_kwo/m/ACC.SG). where, how and how_many are the lexicon's kúdʰe, kʷíh₁ and kʷóti given as closed ids, so they front like the pronouns.

correlative_adv._note: Indeclinable correlative quantifiers answering kʷóti 'how many?': demonstrative *tóti 'so many', relative *h₁yóti 'as many' (Mallory & Adams 2006 §24.2, §24.4). Not fronted.

relative_yo._note: Inflects like so/tod (pronominal -sm- forms). Handbook-standard, UNVERIFIED, except h₁yosméy (dat./loc. sg.), attested in Byrd 2013 (Tier 1).

_refs._engine_sweep_C4: closed-class C4: masc. = neut. in the obliques and dat. pl. = abl. pl. in every pronoun table, masculine primary kept (-oybʰos, -oysōm); Ringe's -oymos/-oysoHom are the alternatives; kʷo-/h₁yo- dat./gen./loc. sg. like so/tod (Ringe p. 55, L&Y §2.2.3)
_refs.personal/1/NOM.SG: engine sweep convention: the -oh₂ form most handbooks print: Fortson §7.4 *eǵoh₂, L&Y Handbook ch. 122 *(h₁)eǵoh₂, Beekes §15.3.1 *h₁eǵ(oH, -Hom); with the table's initial h₁ (Beekes, L&Y, M&A *h₁eĝ-). No book prints the accent: final as in Gk ἐγώ, Ved. ahám. Ringe 2017 p. 57 éǵh₂ and the earlier primary h₁eǵ stay as alternatives
_refs.numerals/indeclinable/10: engine sweep convention: Fortson §7.17 *dék̑m̥, L&Y Handbook ch. 122 *dék̑m̥ (= the lexicon's pie-lex-dekjm and Wiktionary); Beekes §15.4 *dék´mt and Ringe 2017 p. 54 déḱm̥d kept as alternatives
_refs.interrogative_adv/why: the neuter interrogative used adverbially: Ved. kím adv. 'why?' (EWAia I 347 s.v. kí-), Lat. quid, Gk τί 'why?'; Goth. ƕa 'what' = 'why' < *kʷod (Fortson 2010 ch. 15, Gothic text commentary); M&A 2006 §24.3 p. 419 *kʷíd 'what' (Lat. quid, Hitt. kuit)
_refs.interrogative_adv/when: Mallory & Adams 2006 §24.3, Table 24.3 / pp. 419-420 *kʷóm 'when' (Lat. cum, Goth. ƕan, OPr. kan, Alb. kë), 'a special development of the masculine accusative of *kʷós'; Fortson 2010 §7.27 (Archaic Lat. quom 'when, since'); Beekes 2011 p. 250 (cum < quom)
_refs.interrogative_adv/where: Beekes 2011 p. 246 (*-dʰe: Skt kúha, OCS kъde 'where?'); EWAia I 383 s.v. kúha (RV; OAv. kudā); M&A 2006 §24.3 p. 420 *kʷu 'where'; = lexicon pie-lex-kudhe
_refs.interrogative_adv/how: Fortson 2010 §19.10 (*kʷih₁ instr. > Alb. si, Lat. quī 'how'); = interrogative_kwi INS.SG and lexicon pie-lex-kwih1
_refs.interrogative_adv/how_many: Mallory & Adams 2006 §24.3, Table 24.3 / pp. 419-420 *kʷóti ~ *kʷéti (Lat. quot, Skt káti, Gk πόσος; Av. čaiti); EWAia I 294 s.v. káti ('wie viele, quot', RV); = lexicon pie-lex-kwoti
_refs.correlative_adv/so_many: Mallory & Adams 2006 §24.2 / p. 418 *tóti 'so much, many' (Lat. tot, Gk τόσος); Skt táti; = lexicon pie-lex-toti
_refs.correlative_adv/as_many: Mallory & Adams 2006 §24.4 / p. 421 *yóti 'as much, as many' (Skt yáti, Gk ὅσος; Greek and Indo-Iranian only, 'or were created?'); initial h₁ as in relative_yo

anaphoric_i._note: Anaphoric 'he, she, it (just mentioned)' (Lat. is ea id, Ved. ayám iyám idám, Goth. is). Ringe 2017 p. 56 prints the whole sg./pl. paradigm (i-grade in nom./acc./ins., e-grade elsewhere); initial h₁ after Beekes 2011 p. 229 and Mallory & Adams 2006 §24.2. Dual and fem. ins. sg. not reconstructed (Ringe '???'), left out. Ringe also gives an unaccented clitic use (pure anaphora), not modelled here.

deictic_ki._note: Near deictic 'this (here)': Hitt. kā- < *ḱo- (Fortson §9.25; Beekes p. 227; Handbook ch. 21 §5.1), i-stem *ḱi- in OCS sь, Lith. šìs, Goth. himma, Lat. cis (Fortson §7.10; Handbook ch. 116 §5.1 *ḱis). Ringe 2017 p. 56 pairs adnominal *ḱo- with full-NP *ḱi/e- and says the o-stems inflect like the relative. Hittite-attested cells are cited; the rest follow demonstrative_so (see _derived). The i-stem is kept only as an alternative nom. sg. m. *ḱís.

deictic_eno._note: Far deictic 'that (yonder)', stem *h₁eno-/*h₁ono-: Fortson §7.10 *eno- or *ono- (Hitt. ēni-, OCS onŭ; §16.33 Arm. -n, the 'over there' member of the three-way system; §7.29 Gk ekeĩnos < *e-ḱe-eno-); Handbook ch. 21 §5.1 Hitt. anna/i- < *éno-; Handbook ch. 82 (Slavic) §5.1 OCS distal onъ < *h₂en-o-; Beekes §15.2.1 and Mallory & Adams §24.2 *h₂en- (OCS onъ, Lith. anàs). Chosen over *h₂ew- (Beekes only, as a particle 'away'; Handbook ch. 111 §4.3 treats Iranian *au̯a- as a secondary PII formation). h₁ rather than h₂ because Hittite, which keeps h₂ as ḫ-, has none (anna/i-, ēni-); Fortson's vowel-initial *eno- gets h₁ by this table's convention. No book declines it: every cell follows demonstrative_so (see _derived).
